subject: [Project Basalt] Kickoff: in-browser adaptive LMs for accessibility input
body:
Hi team,

Kicking off our on-device predictive-text effort. We're running this under the internal codename Project Basalt — use it in subject lines so the filters catch everything.

Why this matters: the adaptive language models in our open-source JS release are cheap enough, memory- and processor-wise, to train in the browser on the fly. No server round-trips, no data leaving the device — that is exactly the privacy story our accessibility input surface needs, in the tradition of Dasher-style continuous text entry.

Plan for the window (Apr 6 - Jul 27):
- May 8: PPM character model integrated into the input-surface prototype
- Jun 12: adaptation quality study — does per-user on-the-fly training beat the static baseline within one session?
- Jul 15: privacy review complete (I'll file with Kofi this week given the 2-3 week SLA) and LRB packet drafted

Alina, over to you for staffing and any compute needs — should be tiny for this one.

Priya
